## Introduction

This task tested whether humans have a "sixth sense" - the ability to detect when someone is **staring at them** from behind.

You completed **6 trials**:

- Someone either stared at you or looked away
- You guessed which it was
- You rated your confidence (1-10)

**If this is just guessing, you'd expect 50% accuracy.**

::: {.key-finding}
#### Key Finding
Overall accuracy was approximately **52%**, very close to chance levels. This suggests no evidence for a "sixth sense" in this sample.
:::

## Load the Data

## Reshape to Long Format

```{webr-r}
# Reshape data for analysis
stare_long <- sixthsense |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -id,
    names_to = c("trial", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "t(\\d+)_(.+)"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    trial = as.numeric(trial),
    correct = actual == guess
  )

head(stare_long)
```

## Overall Accuracy

What's our detection accuracy?

```{webr-r}
# Calculate accuracy per participant
accuracy_by_person <- stare_long |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(
    n_correct = sum(correct),
    n_trials = n(),
    accuracy = n_correct / n_trials
  )

accuracy_by_person
```

## Compare to Chance

```{webr-r}
# Overall accuracy
overall_accuracy <- mean(stare_long$correct)
cat("Overall accuracy:", scales::percent(overall_accuracy), "\n")
cat("Chance level: 50%\n")

# Visualise
ggplot(accuracy_by_person, aes(x = accuracy)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1/6, fill = "#9b59b6", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "#e74c3c", linewidth = 1.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.52, y = 2.5, label = "Chance (50%)",
           hjust = 0, color = "#e74c3c", size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Accuracy",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Individual Detection Accuracy",
    subtitle = "Are you better than chance?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#275882")
  )
```

## Statistical Test: Do We Have a Sixth Sense?

```{webr-r}
# One-sample t-test against chance (0.5)
t_result <- t.test(accuracy_by_person$accuracy, mu = 0.5)
t_result
```

```{webr-r}
# Interpretation
if (t_result$p.value < 0.05) {
  cat("Result: We performed SIGNIFICANTLY different from chance!\n")
  if (t_result$estimate > 0.5) {
    cat("We appear to have some detection ability.\n")
  } else {
    cat("Interestingly, we performed WORSE than chance.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Result: No evidence of sixth sense - performance at chance level.\n")
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## What Does This Mean?

The "sixth sense" or "gaze detection" is a popular belief, but scientific evidence is mixed:

- **Believers** point to studies showing slightly above-chance detection
- **Skeptics** note that positive results often fail to replicate
- **Methodological issues** include experimenter effects and confirmation bias

Our data suggests **no evidence** for a sixth sense in this controlled setting. This is consistent with the idea that our "feeling of being watched" may be a **cognitive illusion** rather than a real sensory ability.
:::

## Confidence and Accuracy

Do people who are more confident perform better?

```{webr-r}
# Relationship between confidence and accuracy
conf_accuracy <- stare_long |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(
    mean_confidence = mean(conf, na.rm = TRUE),
    accuracy = mean(correct)
  )

ggplot(conf_accuracy, aes(x = mean_confidence, y = accuracy)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#9b59b6") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#275882") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "#e74c3c") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    x = "Mean Confidence Rating",
    y = "Accuracy",
    title = "Does Confidence Predict Accuracy?",
    subtitle = "Red line = chance performance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold")
  )
```

```{webr-r}
# Correlation test
cor.test(conf_accuracy$mean_confidence, conf_accuracy$accuracy)
```

## Signal Detection: Hits and False Alarms

Let's analyse this using signal detection theory:

- **Hit**: Correctly detecting staring
- **Miss**: Failing to detect staring
- **False Alarm**: Saying "staring" when they weren't
- **Correct Rejection**: Correctly saying "not staring"

```{webr-r}
# Calculate signal detection metrics
sdt_data <- stare_long |>
  mutate(
    response_type = case_when(
      actual == 1 & guess == 1 ~ "Hit",
      actual == 1 & guess == 2 ~ "Miss",
      actual == 2 & guess == 1 ~ "False Alarm",
      actual == 2 & guess == 2 ~ "Correct Rejection"
    )
  )

sdt_summary <- sdt_data |>
  count(response_type) |>
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n))

ggplot(sdt_summary, aes(x = response_type, y = n, fill = response_type)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Hit" = "#27ae60",
                                "Miss" = "#e74c3c",
                                "False Alarm" = "#f39c12",
                                "Correct Rejection" = "#3498db")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Count",
    title = "Signal Detection Analysis",
    subtitle = "Types of responses"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold")
  )
```

## Bonus: Accuracy by Trial

```{webr-r}
trial_accuracy <- stare_long |>
  group_by(trial) |>
  summarise(
    accuracy = mean(correct),
    se = sd(correct) / sqrt(n())
  )

ggplot(trial_accuracy, aes(x = trial, y = accuracy)) +
  geom_line(color = "#9b59b6", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "#9b59b6", size = 4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = accuracy - se, ymax = accuracy + se),
              alpha = 0.2, fill = "#9b59b6") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "#e74c3c", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Trial",
    y = "Accuracy",
    title = "Detection Accuracy Across Trials",
    subtitle = "Red line = chance level (50%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold")
  )
```

---

::: {.key-finding}
#### Summary

The data shows **no evidence** for a "sixth sense" - detection accuracy was not significantly different from chance (50%). Additionally, confidence did not predict accuracy, suggesting people lack insight into when their guesses are correct.
:::
